div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 1000px; text-align: center;

span.div:
Reduce contention: finer-grained locks, shorter
critical sections
Improve throughput: shard lock namespace, cache lock
state
Multi-region: leader region, resource affinity, async
replication
Monitor: hold duration, contention ratio, lease expiry
rate

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 1000px; text-align: center;

span.div:
TTL expiry while holding: fencing token or abort
Clock drift: monotonic clocks, tolerance buffer
Network partition: lease timeout, fencing token
protection
Server crash: TTL auto-release, eventual consistency

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 1000px; text-align: center;

span.div:
Lock acquisition: atomic check-and-set with TTL
Lock release: safe (owner check) release
Fencing tokens: monotonic token per grant
Lease renewal: periodic heartbeat or TTL extension
Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 1000px; text-align: center;

span.div:
Redis (1-3ms): non-critical, high throughput, tolerant
of failures
ZooKeeper (5-15ms): critical, consistency required,
lower throughput
etcd (3-8ms): Kubernetes-native, leases, Raft
consensus
Database (10-100ms): existing infra, low throughput,
coarse locks

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 1000px; text-align: center;

span.div:
Do multiple processes access a shared resource
concurrently?
Can concurrent access cause data corruption or
duplicate work?
Is idempotency or optimistic concurrency insufficient?
